thread:
incident-bot: PAGER ALERT — P1: embeddings-reranker pipeline errors for /batch-rerank endpoint. Error rate spike >80% since 11:07 UTC. Paging oncall.
alice: on it. getting logs now. assigning myself as incident lead. @carol can you set incident channel to #incidents and start a timeline? :eyes:
carol: on it — created timeline doc and postmortem stub. link: https://internal/redwood/incidents/1719001234 (placeholder)
bob: seeing 500s from reranker workers in logs (reranker-v2). errors look like: "vector_size_mismatch: expected 1024 got 2048". copying snippets below.
carol: can you paste the full log block? also ping infra if this is a deploy issue.
bob: log (excerpt):
```
2024-05-21T11:09:12Z ERROR reranker.worker RequestID=abc123: failed to score batch: vector_size_mismatch: expected=1024 received=2048
2024-05-21T11:09:12Z ERROR reranker.api RequestID=abc123: downstream error: faiss_index_build_failed: InvalidArgument
2024-05-21T11:09:12Z WARN reranker.api Batch endpoint returning 400 to client
```
alice: helpful. what released recently? @dmitri any out-of-hours deploys to reranker or embedding model? dmitri: there was a config-only rollout at 10:55 UTC for embedding model v3.4.2 -> swapped weight file path, but CI said dims unchanged. however infra also deployed a packaging change to embedding-serving image at 10:58 UTC (small PR: use new tokenizer lib).
emma: Customer success seeing multiple support tickets for failures in bulk import/rerank jobs. Count so far: 7 customers reported errors, 2 of them high-volume (enterprise) — flagged as customer-impacting.
bob: running a quick local check: the embedding model in the new image prints shape (2048) for token embeddings when run with --export-dim flag. older image prints 1024. suspect model binary swapped in with different output dim.
carol: mitigation idea: route /batch-rerank traffic to fallback reranker cluster that expects 2048 until we sort models. Can we do that quickly? alice: we can change smart-routing rule to region-fallback -> point traffic to reranker-canary group (already configured). Doing now — gate for 5m to observe.
incident-bot: ACTION TAKEN: routing change applied at 11:18 UTC. % of requests routed to canary cluster: 100%.
alice: monitoring errors and latency. errors drop to ~3% on fallback cluster. original cluster still logging vector_size_mismatch.
dmitri: investigating image lineage — found tag mismatch: embedding-serving:prod:20240521-1152 actually built from model export pipeline that produced 2048-dim vectors. build metadata link: s3://redwood-builds/embeddings/20240521/metadata.json
bob: hypothesis tracking:
  HYPOTHESIS A: model export pipeline produced a 2048-d matrix but serving config still expects 1024 — config/model mismatch.
  HYPOTHESIS B: serialization bug in tokenizer changed embedding shape in-edge case.
  HYPOTHESIS C: client-side contract changed (unlikely) — batch client sending additional fields.
alice: label HYPOTHESIS A as highest priority. bob please confirm by fetching model metadata and config files. carol, make a list of impacted customers and mitigation comms.
bob: fetched metadata: model: embedder-v2.1 export_dim: 2048. serving-config (prod) expected_dim: 1024. patch applied in image build mistakenly used latest export without bumping config. diff snippet:
```
- expected_dim: 1024
+ expected_dim: 1024  # not updated
# model artifact: embedder-v2.1 -> export_dim: 2048
```
carol: impact assessment: 7 customers failed during 11:07-11:18 window. 2 high-volume saw partial import failures (some batches retried). We sent initial comms to affected customers at 11:30 UTC.
emma: customers appreciate quick update, asked for ETA for full resolution and for logs of failed batches. we can provide S3 paths.
alice: mitigation path: we have two safe options:
  1) roll back embedding-serving image to previous build (1024) — risk: rollback of other non-related fixes in image.
  2) patch serving-config to accept 2048 vectors and do an index rebuild on side cluster — risk: index time, temporary higher CPU.
We applied routing to fallback cluster to restore customer traffic. next step: roll back embedder image on prod cluster to stop further mis-exports.
dmitri: started rollback job on prod embedding-serving at 11:25 UTC (kubectl rollout restart --image=embedding-serving:20240520-2230). monitoring.
carol: timeline update: 11:07 first error spike, 11:09 reranker logs show vector_size_mismatch, 11:18 routing to fallback, 11:25 rollback started, 11:32 rollback finished and tests OK, 11:34 fallback routing disabled -> traffic back to primary cluster.
alice: post-rollback checks: run curl health endpoints and run small rerank smoke test (provided test payload). smoke test passed at 11:35. errors drop to baseline <0.1%.
bob: root cause hypothesis confirmed: build pipeline picked up a newer model artifact with export_dim changed to 2048. CI didn't assert export_dim compatibility with serving-config. missing invariant check.
carol: action items we agreed on in-thread:
  - (owner: bob) Add CI check that export_dim == serving-config.expected_dim for builds that package model artifacts. (ETA: 48h)
  - (owner: dmitri) Add model artifact signing / manifest verification in image build so mismatch fails early. (ETA: 1 week)
  - (owner: alice) Postmortem writeup + customer summary + timeline. (ETA: 24h)
  - (owner: carol) Run replay tests for batch endpoints and add regression test for reranker for embedding dim mismatches. (ETA: 72h)
  - (owner: emma) Follow-up customer comms + provide per-customer failed batch logs. (ETA: 3h)
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS changed -> RESOLVED at 11:40 UTC (root cause identified, rollback applied, customer traffic restored).
alice: brief notes for RCA: root cause = model export pipeline regression allowed a 2048-dim model artifact into prod image without updating serving-config. Contributing factors: missing CI guard, lack of artifact manifest verification, and no dimension contract check in reranker at startup.
bob: potential preventative: have serving process fail-fast when received vectors of unexpected dim (currently returns 400). Instead, we should log and emit metric and fail the deploy if startup verification fails. will file PR.
carol: I'm creating the formal postmortem doc and will include timeline/log snippets/commands used. Will schedule a blameless review tomorrow 15:00 UTC.
emma: customers notified with timeline + remediation steps. will coordinate targeted follow-ups.
alice: closing notes: great cross-team response, routing fallback saved most customers. main follow-ups are CI/build fixes and server-side dim checks. marking thread for RCA doc merge.
carol: assigning follow-up tickets now: https://internal/redwood/tickets/INC-1719001234-rca
alice: thanks team. :slightly_smiling_face:\"
